sector_model: subscription consumer software with hardware and advertising: judged on paying circle and ARPPC growth, gross margin, GAAP pretax income separate from tax benefits, free cash flow with and without stock compensation, convertible debt against cash, acquisition effects; EV/Adjusted EBITDA is management context only
thesis: Life360 (Nasdaq: LIF; also ASX: 360) sells a family location and safety app. Q3 2026 revenue 174.1M (+40%), 9M 476.2M vs 343.5M (+39%); subscription 124.2M (+29%), advertising 25.4M vs 7.3M (Nativo acquired, about 57.1M cash paid), paying circles 3.4M (+26%), MAU 107.7M (+17%), subscription gross margin 87%. FY2026 guidance raised at the midpoint: revenue 665 to 681M, Adjusted EBITDA 132 to 138M (about 20% margin). Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 333.1M plus short-term investments 129.2M, 320M principal of 0% convertible notes due 2030 (conversion about 80.97, carrying value 312.0M), total liabilities 455.1M, equity 630.6M. TTM (FY2025 plus 9M 2026 minus 9M 2025): revenue 622.2M, OCF 104.95M, capex (PP&E 0.45M plus capitalized software 4.97M) 5.4M, FCF about 99.5M, stock compensation about 74.7M so FCF after SBC about 24.8M. At the verified 2026-11-10 close of 41.98 and 81.755M shares (cover, 2026-11-03) market cap is about 3.43B; EV about 3.29B using cash and investments of 462.4M less 320M convertible principal is about 3.29B (3.43B plus 320M less 462M). Multiples: about 24x FY2026 guided Adjusted EBITDA midpoint, FCF yield 2.9% (0.7% after SBC). GAAP TTM net income of 160.0M gives 21x but is not earnings power: FY2025 carried an income tax benefit of 118.2M (valuation allowance release) and 9M 2026 a further 9.7M benefit; TTM pretax income is only 32.3M, including fair value gains on investments and interest income, so tax-normalized earnings at 21% are about 25M (about 135x). Price fell 6.7% on 2026-11-10 after the 11-09 release (45.02 to 41.98); cause not confirmed from the call.
counterthesis: GAAP profit is thin: 9M 2026 operating income was -0.2M on 476.2M revenue, TTM pretax income 32.3M, and reported net income depends on a large deferred tax asset (143.2M) and a 17.5M non-operating fair value gain in Q3. Stock compensation (59.2M in 9M, 12% of revenue) is nearly as large as FCF, so FCF after SBC is under 1% of market cap. Advertising growth is largely acquired (Nativo) and its guidance range was narrowed down (98 to 102M from 98 to 115M); hardware units fell 32% after exiting brick-and-mortar retail; advertising gross margin is low (Q3 cost 11.5M on 25.4M revenue). Q3 OCF 27.2M was below Adjusted EBITDA 34.6M. Related party and Aura arrangements are growing (related party revenue, deferred revenue and fair value gains). Convertible notes are 0% with a conversion price near 81 against a 42 stock, so they are debt not equity for now; maturity 2030. Competition from Apple and Google location features and Tile-related privacy litigation (arbitration compelled, no accrual). Share count rose 2.8% from year-end despite 44.4M of buybacks. Revenue growth of 36 to 39% must continue to justify about 24x Adjusted EBITDA.
invalidation: Paying circle net additions falling below about 100 thousand per quarter or subscription growth below about 20%; subscription gross margin below 83%; GAAP operating income staying near zero while SBC exceeds 12% of revenue; advertising revenue growth stalling after the Nativo comparison; FCF before SBC below about 50M; further large non-operating gains or tax items driving net income.
